name: LTC4151IMS#PBF
title: High voltage I2C current and voltage monitor
summary: The LTC4151 is a high side power monitor for rails from 7 V to 80 V. A 12-bit ADC converts the voltage across an external shunt (81.92 mV full scale), the supply voltage on VIN (102.4 V full scale) and one spare input, ADIN (2.048 V full scale), and a host reads the results over I2C, either from a continuous scan or from single snapshot conversions. The LTC4151 has a shutdown pin; the LTC4151-1 (inverted) and LTC4151-2 split the I2C data line into input and output for driving opto-isolators.
key_figures: 1.2 mA typ (48 V); 120 µA typ in shutdown (12 V)

circuits.title: High side power sensing with onboard ADC and I2C
circuits.description: A 0.02 Ω shunt in the positive supply line feeds SENSE+ and SENSE-, giving 4.096 A full scale. VIN and ADR1 sit on the input rail and ADR0 on ground, which selects address CEh (Table 1). ADIN takes the voltage to be measured, ~SHDN is an input from outside, and SCL and SDA go to a 3.3 V microcontroller with 2 kΩ pull-ups to its supply.

circuits.title: Figure 1. Monitoring high side current and voltages
circuits.description: The basic hook-up. The 0.02 Ω shunt between the input rail and VOUT sets 4.096 A full scale on the SENSE channel; VIN is read to 102.4 V full scale and ADIN to 2.048 V. ADR1 to the input rail and ADR0 to ground give address CEh. ~SHDN is left open, so the part runs. SCL and SDA have 2 kΩ pull-ups to the microcontroller's 3.3 V.

circuits.title: Figure 9. Opto-isolated I2C between LTC4151-1 and a microcontroller
circuits.description: A 48 V supply runs through a 0.02 Ω shunt. Two MOCD207M dual opto-couplers carry the bus across an isolation barrier. On the host side, 0.51 kΩ resistors from 3.3 V feed the two LEDs of U2, whose cathodes are the host's SCL and SDA lines (10 kΩ pull-ups); U2's transistors pull the LTC4151-1's SCL and SDAI low, with 20 kΩ pull-ups to the monitored rail. The inverted ~SDAO output, pulled up through 5.1 kΩ, drives the LED of U3 directly: when ~SDAO releases, the LED lights and U3's transistor pulls the host's SDA low. With the LED of U3 clamping ~SDAO and the internal 6 V clamps on SCL and SDAI, all three pull-ups return to the monitored rail and no separate low-voltage supply is needed. ADR1 high and ADR0 low select address CEh.

parts.note: dual opto-coupler, LTC4151-1 to host; second channel unused

notes: The I2C data rate is about 1.5 kHz, set by the slew rate of the opto-isolators.

circuits.title: LTC4151-1 on a -48 V system with an opto-isolated microcontroller
circuits.description: The Figure 9 arrangement on a negative supply: the LTC4151-1 is referred to the -48 V rail, which is its GND, and RTN is its VIN. The 0.02 Ω shunt sits in the RTN line, so the part reads the return current and the input voltage. Two MOCD207M opto-couplers carry SCL and SDAI in and the inverted ~SDAO out to a 3.3 V microcontroller on its own ground; the LTC-side pull-ups (20 kΩ, 20 kΩ, 5.1 kΩ) return to the load side of the shunt. ADR1 to RTN and ADR0 to -48 V give address CEh.

parts.note: dual opto-coupler, LTC4151-1 to host; second channel unused

notes: The I2C data rate is about 1.5 kHz, set by the slew rate of the opto-isolators.

circuits.title: Figure 11. LTC4151-2 opto-isolated I2C with high speed opto-couplers
circuits.description: For faster bus speeds the non-inverting LTC4151-2 talks through two PS9817-2 high-speed dual opto-couplers. An LT3010-5 regulator, fed from VIN (1 µF 100 V in, 1 µF out), makes a local 5 V that powers ISO2 and the LTC-side pull-ups (10 kΩ on SCL and SDAI) and, through R8 (1 kΩ), the LED of ISO1. SDAO sinks ISO1's LED cathode, and ISO1's output drives ISO_SDA on the isolated side. ISO2's two LEDs are driven from the isolated 5 V through 1 kΩ resistors with ISO_SDA and ISO_SCL as their cathode returns; its outputs drive SDAI and SCL. ISO_SDA and ISO_SCL have 10 kΩ pull-ups to the isolated 5 V, which is bypassed by 0.1 µF. Both address pins are grounded, address DEh. If the host keeps its SDA in and out apart, the acknowledge bit from SDAO has to be returned to SDAI.

circuits.title: Temperature monitoring with an NTC thermistor while measuring load current and LTC4151 supply current
circuits.description: A 48 V rail feeds a 250 mA load through a 0.2 Ω shunt. The VIN pin is taken from the load side of the shunt, so the measured current includes the LTC4151's own supply current. A divider from the 48 V input, made of a 100 kΩ (at 25°C, 1%) NTC thermistor, 40.2 kΩ and 1.5 kΩ (both 1%), puts a temperature-dependent fraction of the rail on ADIN. Temperature follows from the ratio of the ADIN and VIN codes (equation 'NTC thermistor temperature'). Both address pins are grounded, address DEh.
notes: The temperature equation holds from 20°C to 60°C.

circuits.title: High side current, input voltage and open fuse monitoring with a single LTC4151
circuits.description: Two 48 V feeds, each through its own fuse (F1, F2), are diode-ORed by D1 and D2 into the LTC4151's VIN and a 0.02 Ω shunt to the load. A second path from each fuse's output, through D3 with 150 kΩ and D4 with 301 kΩ, joins at ADIN with 3.4 kΩ to ground. The ADIN code against the VIN code then tells which fuse, if any, has opened (table 'Open fuse detection by code ratio'). Both address pins are grounded, address DEh.
notes: VIN1 and VIN2 are to be within 20% of each other.

operation.text: The LTC4151 runs from 7 V to 80 V and draws under 1.7 mA in normal operation. A 12-bit delta-sigma ADC with an internal 2.048 V reference reads, one after another, the drop across a high side shunt (SENSE+ to SENSE-, through an internal sense amplifier), the VIN pin (through an internal divider), and the ADIN pin. Results sit in on-chip registers that a host reads over I2C.

Pulling ~SHDN under 1 V puts the LTC4151 into shutdown, cutting supply current to under 300 µA (120 µA typical). The pin has an internal pull-up to 6.3 V; open means running. The -1 and -2 versions use this pin for ~SDAO and have no shutdown.

After power-up the ADC cycles through SENSE, then VIN, then ADIN without stopping, and registers A to F refresh at 7.5 Hz. Each result takes two adjacent registers: the 8 MSBs in the first, the 4 LSBs in the upper half of the second. The delta-sigma converter averages noise over each conversion. The busy bits stay at 0 in this mode.

For a single on-demand reading, write the control register with G7 = 1 and the channel code in G6:G5 (00 SENSE, 01 VIN, 10 ADIN) using a Write Byte. The busy bit in that channel's LSB register goes to 1 during the conversion and returns to 0 when the result is valid; the ADC then stops. To convert again, on the same or another channel, first clear G7, then set it again with the new channel code. Conversion takes 67 ms typical for SENSE and 33 ms for VIN or ADIN.
Setting G4 halts the ADC and makes data registers A to F writable, so software can write known values and read them back.

The part is an I2C read-write slave with six data registers and one control register. It accepts the SMBus commands Write Byte, Read Byte, Write Word and Read Word, plus Read Page and Write Page for longer transfers. During word and page transfers the register pointer steps by one after each byte, wraps from 06h to 00h, and goes back to 00h at a Stop. Clearing G3 turns page transfers off.

The three-state ADR0 and ADR1 pins (high, low or open) choose one of nine 7-bit addresses whose top bits a6:a4 are 110 (Table 1). Every LTC4151 also answers the mass-write address 1100 110 (CCh with the write bit), whatever its pins say.

An idle bus has SCL and SDA both high. Start is SDA falling while SCL is high; Stop is SDA rising while SCL is high. The transmitter lets SDA go during the ninth clock and the receiver pulls it low to acknowledge. If the LTC4151 leaves SDA high the host may end with a Stop. When reading, the host acknowledges each byte it wants followed by another, and leaves SDA high after the last before sending Stop.

Start, 7-bit address with R/W = 0, acknowledge, then a command byte whose lower three bits load the register pointer, acknowledge, then data. Each data byte is acknowledged and stored at the pointer, which advances for Write Word and Write Page. A Stop ends the write and resets the pointer to 00h.

Start, address with R/W = 0, command byte to set the pointer, then a repeated Start and the same address with R/W = 1. The LTC4151 acknowledges and returns the addressed register. Each host acknowledge brings the next register (Read Word, Read Page). A Stop ends the read and resets the pointer to 00h.

A timer runs whenever SCL or SDA/SDAI is low and resets once both are high. If either stays low for more than 33 ms (typical; 20 ms minimum) the internal I2C state machine resets, so the bus works again once the fault clears. Clearing G2 disables the timer.

The -1 and -2 split data into SDAI in and a separate open-drain output for a host on another ground: inverted ~SDAO on the -1, plain SDAO on the -2. With the -1, SDAI is driven by the incoming opto-coupler and ~SDAO drives the anode of the outgoing one. Since the outgoing LED clamps ~SDAO, and SDAI and SCL carry internal 6 V clamps (5.5 V minimum), all three pull-ups may go straight to VIN and no low-voltage supply is needed. Slow opto-couplers limit the bus to about 1.5 kHz (Figure 9); the -2 with high-speed opto-couplers and a local 5 V regulator runs faster (Figure 11). If the host's SDA input and output are separate, the acknowledge from SDAO must be passed back to SDAI.

Route SENSE+ and SENSE- as Kelvin connections to the pads of the sense resistor RS (Figure 10), separate from the high-current path between VIN and the load. For 1 oz copper the current-carrying traces need at least 0.02 inch of width per amp; 0.03 inch per amp or more is recommended. 1 oz copper has a sheet resistance of about 530 µΩ per square.
